spatial_claims.claim: Point C lies on segment AB, found by applying 6.28 to obtain AC * CB = r^3/(4s)
D lies on the semicircle described on diameter AB
Angle ADB in the semicircle is a right angle (by 3.31)
Triangle ADB has a right angle at D, so AD^2 + DB^2 = AB^2 (by 1.47)
CD is the altitude from D to hypotenuse AB, giving CD^2 = AC * CB, AD^2 = AC * AB, DB^2 = CB * AB (by 6.8)
rect(AD, DB) = rect(AB, CD) from area of triangle computed two ways
M is the midpoint of AB; AC * CB + MC^2 = (AB/2)^2 (by 2.5)

configuration_map: Configuration: Semicircle on diameter AB. Point C on segment AB between A and B. Perpendicular CD from C meets semicircle at D above AB. AD and DB joined to form right triangle ADB (right angle at D by 3.31). CD serves as the altitude from the right-angle vertex D to hypotenuse AB. M is the midpoint of AB. All subsequent algebraic reasoning (Steps 7-16) uses the relations CD^2 = AC*CB, AD^2 = AC*AB, DB^2 = CB*AB, and AD*DB = AB*CD derived from this standard configuration. The configuration is entirely standard (semicircle with inscribed right triangle and altitude to hypotenuse) and all spatial claims are mutually consistent throughout the proof.
pass_reason: The geometric configuration is a standard semicircle construction with an inscribed right triangle and altitude to the hypotenuse. All spatial claims (point positions, perpendicularity, right angle, altitude relations, area equality, midpoint identity) are mutually consistent. The proof is predominantly algebraic, manipulating commensurability relations using Book 10 propositions; the geometric construction merely establishes the algebraic relations and does so correctly. No spatial configuration contradiction exists.
